$comment: RAY-CLOUD shared contract 1.0.0-rc.1. CLI verb map, result envelope and exit codes. Codes and their exit classes are in error-codes.json.

output.rule: A new verb writes exactly one final JSON envelope to stdout, with or without --json. While it runs, stdout carries nothing else: progress, library and runtime output go to stderr, and so does the short human-readable description of the result, which is written only without --json. An existing verb without --json keeps its current output byte for byte. An existing verb with --json writes the envelope with its legacy result object unchanged in data and adds the warning RAY_W_LEGACY_OUTPUT; its legacy string errors become errors with code RAY_CHECK_FAILED and the string as message, and its spec errors become SPEC_ codes.
output.secrets: No output, log, error message or envelope field ever carries a secret value, a bindings-file value, an identity or key file content, or a path component known to be secret.
output.operationId: A new verb generates a fresh random UUID v4 operationId per invocation and always prints it on stderr as "operationId: <id>", with or without --json. An existing verb generates and prints one only with --json, so its plain output stays byte for byte as before. A verb records its operationId in any receipt it writes. A runtime.<name> result echoes the operationId of its request, which the caller chose and reuses on retry (runtime-control.md "Common shapes").
output.interrupt: On SIGINT or SIGTERM a verb stops at a safe point, leaves any fence it took in place, writes an envelope with RAY_INTERRUPTED and exits 6. The message carries the recovery instruction: a verb that took a fence names rayspec resume with the deployment and the fence epoch; a passive verb (bundle inspect, bundle verify) or a verb that changed nothing says so and that the command can be run again, and names no rayspec resume because nothing was fenced.

exitCodes.existingVerbs: Existing verbs keep 0, 1 and 2 for every outcome they had in the previous release. An unexpected internal error exits 7 (it exited 2 before this release). Codes 3 to 6 appear on an existing verb only for an outcome that verb did not have before, such as RAY_LOCK_TIMEOUT when the boot waits on the shared advisory lock.

globalFlags.description: Accepted on every verb except tenant recover-owner, which writes its own JSON object once and refuses --json with exit 2. New verbs always write the envelope; the flag is accepted for symmetry.

deployDispatch.rule: rayspec deploy <path> selects the bundle path when the file starts with the ZIP signature 50 4B 03 04 or 50 4B 05 06, or when the path ends in .ray (ASCII case-insensitive). The check reads at most the first 4 bytes and runs before any configuration is loaded or any database connection is opened. A .ray path whose bytes are not a ZIP is refused with RAY_INVALID_ARCHIVE reason not-a-zip. Every other file takes the legacy YAML path.
deployDispatch.legacyOrder: The legacy YAML path validates the spec and signer key before applying the platform migration chain; a spec that fails validation leaves the database untouched, and the exit code stays 1.

Where a verb pipeline lists reader steps it runs them in this order, and on any disagreement 01-RAY-BUNDLE.md governs.

verbs.orderRule: No database connection is opened and no configuration is loaded until the archive, manifest, spec, bindings and signer key have validated. No database mutation happens until the plan is accepted. The shared advisory lock is held for every schema mutation.
verbs.jsonRule: With --json, stdout carries exactly one envelope, written when the process refuses or stops; banners and logs go to stderr.

verbs.summary: Precheck, quiesce under operator confirmation, and write an encrypted complete snapshot as a migration .ray. Never writes plaintext output. Leaves the source fenced, except after a refusal at the precheck, which runs before the fence.

verbs.precheckRule: The precheck runs before the fence and changes nothing. It rebuilds the active application bundle from its version directory and reads it again through the deploy pipeline of this runtime, reader steps 1 to 16 (no signature file lies beside the rebuilt archive), so every code of those steps can refuse an export; a rebuilt archive whose SHA-256 differs from the deployed one is RAY_DIGEST_MISMATCH reason bundle-sha256. It also refuses a source with no organization (RAY_USAGE), more than one (RAY_MULTI_TENANT_UNSUPPORTED), no active member holding a password (RAY_OWNER_RECOVERY_REQUIRED), a database extension other than those the workflow engine creates in its own database (RAY_POLICY_DENIED reason unsupported-extension), a database server major it cannot state (RAY_TARGET_UNSUPPORTED), more than 500,000 objects (RAY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED reason object-index-size), and, when database role separation is not enabled and --source-stopped is not given, the missing database barrier (RAY_EXTERNAL_STATE_UNSUPPORTED reason database-barrier-unavailable). A refusal at the precheck leaves the source unfenced.
verbs.environment: DATABASE_URL (the runtime role), RAYSPEC_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL (role separation), RAYSPEC_SNAPSHOT_DATABASE_URL (the read-only snapshot role), DBOS_SYSTEM_DATABASE_URL, RAYSPEC_BLOB_ROOT and RAYSPEC_PG_DUMP (absolute path of pg_dump; default pg_dump on PATH, of the server's major), from the process environment only, never a .env file.
verbs.leaseRule: The fence is taken and released under the operation lease (runtime-control.md "Operation lease"): RAY_LOCK_TIMEOUT while another operation holds it, RAY_FENCE_MISMATCH when the export's lease expired or was taken over before it finished.

verbs.modeRule: --discard-failed, --cutover-token and --renew-cutover-token are three separate steps; each takes --target alone (any other flag or a positional is RAY_USAGE), and two of them together are RAY_USAGE. The import prints the cutover token once, on stderr, with the instruction to cut over; the envelope never carries it (its data is closed), and the receipts record only its SHA-256. The token works once, for 15 minutes.
